text:
olivia: hitting a flaky case in go/js samples where mid-stream auth refresh truncates a JSON event. Browser shows split data events -> parse error.

ben: minimal repro?

olivia: start 30s stream, reduce token TTL, force refresh at ~25s. sometimes last data event is split across two SSE data frames and when fetch aborts we get a partial buffer and throw.

sam: sounds like parser isn't preserving partial event on abort. node/python keep socket open longer so less likely.

ben: quick fixes: 1) SDK parser: buffer partial data events and only error when stream closes with leftover bytes; 2) sample apps: add a small grace window on auth-refresh abort (opt-in flag) to let micro-chunks arrive; 3) runtime: consider tagging FINAL chunks so they can be retried on reconnect.

olivia: i'll open tiny PR to stop throwing on partial JSON until stream close, add unit tests for split-chunk case. will also add README note for grace flag.

ci-bot: created task DEVEX-2410 and queued parser tests.

sam: later: we should extend resume token to include chunk seq or byte offset so server can resend missing final bytes. add to runtime backlog.

ben: agreed. for now prioritize parser fix + sample workaround and add cross-sdk parity test.

olivia: on it, thanks.
